text:
jay: Heads up — I followed the Python quickstart today and hit multiple issues. The async example uses `AsyncClient` but the link to the async client page 404s, and the snippet itself awaits `client.generate_stream(...)` which doesn't exist on the async client in the installed wheel.

nina: Oof. Can you paste the snippet you used?

jay: Sure — copied from docs: 

```python
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
    async for chunk in client.generate_stream(model_name='gpt-medium', prompt='Hello'):
        print(chunk.text)

asyncio.run(main())
```

This raises AttributeError: 'AsyncClient' object has no attribute 'generate_stream'.

nina: That sounds like API drift. Our async API exposes `stream_generate` not `generate_stream` (naming change during 0.9 refactor). Also PyPI currently has 0.9.2 but some internal deps still pin 0.8.x which used the other shapes.

qa: doc-bot reported linkcheck failure in the last build: `/docs/quickstart/python` -> 404 on `/docs/clients/python/async`. Log: `LinkCheck: GET /docs/clients/python/async -> 404`.

eng-runtime: We intentionally renamed `generate_stream` -> `stream_generate` for parity with the sync client earlier this quarter. Docs should have been updated but looks like the quickstart slipped. We didn't add an alias because stream functions are tricky w/ typing and awaitables.

jay: Two user-facing suggestions: 1) Update the quickstart snippet to call `stream_generate` and add a tiny note that streaming is an async iterator. 2) Add a short compatibility note for folks on 0.8.x (or pin the quickstart to the exact tested version).

leo: I can update the docs, but can we also add a small validated example under `examples/python/quickstart_async.py` in the docs repo and run it as part of the docs smoke test? If we run the snippet in a minimal venv (pip install -U redwood-inference==${PIN}), we'll catch API drift earlier.

nina: +1. Also, typing breakages: migrating to typed clients flagged a bunch of mypy/pyright warnings in internal scripts because old wrapper helpers were `Any`-less. We should add a one-paragraph "Typing & upgrade notes" in the quickstart describing typical fixes: annotate responses as `Response`, use `ResponseChoice` for choices, and show `from redwood import AsyncClient, Response` example.

eng-runtime: Agreed. But note: we cannot change runtime names now without wider rollout. Docs update + clear changelog entry is lower risk.

doc-bot: Automated deploy attempt: failed linkcheck for `/docs/quickstart/python` (403 on /docs/clients/python/async) at 2024-10-21T09:14:03Z

jay: I opened internal ticket RW-8123 with repro steps and attached my console output and the snippet I used.

leo: I'll push PR to docs to: update snippet (use `stream_generate`), add 'Typing & upgrade notes' section, and pin the quickstart TOC to show the tested package version (e.g., "Tested with: redwood-inference==0.9.2"). Will also add a docs CI job to run the example under 3.10/3.11.

nina: Small UX ask — can the Python wheel's runtime also emit a deprecation warning for `generate_stream` if we decide to add a tiny compatibility wrapper (only if we implement a short-lived alias)? That would help users during the transition.

eng-runtime: We can add a shim with a DeprecationWarning for one release cycle. I'll open an RFC for the change and link it to the docs PR.

doc-bot: docs deploy succeeded for branch docs/quickstart-async-fixes at 2024-11-05T18:27:12Z

qa: After the fix landed, I ran the new docs CI job. It failed initially because the example used `os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')` with an empty key and the client raised a hard exception. I tweaked the example runner to set a fake key and skip network calls (use `REDWOOD_SKIP_NETWORK=1` in the env to exercise import/runtime shapes only).

leo: Good catch. I updated the example runner to set `REDWOOD_KEY=fake` and `REDWOOD_SKIP_NETWORK=1` (docs CI uses a small unit test harness, not real API). The smoke test now validates the snippet imports and method names for 3.10/3.11.

jay: Thanks all. Leaving a note for support: if you see users hit AttributeError on `generate_stream` or `generate`, point them to RW-8123 and the updated quickstart (docs link: https://docs.redwood.com/quickstart/python — should be updated). :raised_hands:
